questionText: What is the difference between idempotency and safety in HTTP?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can apply the separate safety and idempotency tests and classify common HTTP methods without confusing read intent with repeatability.

claims.statement: Safety concerns whether the client requested a state change, while idempotency concerns the intended effect of repeating the same request.
GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE are safe; safe methods plus PUT and DELETE are idempotent under their standard semantics.

examples.title: Unsafe cancellation hidden behind GET compared with POST

validation.expected: The GET example visibly violates safe semantics

visuals.title: Safety and idempotency as separate axes

notes: Incidental logging and metrics are distinguished from a state change requested by the client.

review.notes: The method classifications were checked against RFC 9110; editorial and rendered-table review remain open.
